LESSON: ECONOMIC ACTIVITIES IN THE COUNTY

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Resources and Economic Activities
Topic 4.1: Economic activities in the County

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Economic activities in the County. Read, look at the pictures, practise, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: LEARN

RESOURCES IN THE COUNTY  Today we shall talk about resources in the county. We shall talk about resources in the county. 

Welcome to our social studies lesson. In this lesson we shall learn about resources in the county. We shall also learn how we can conserve the resources in our County. Learner, What are resources? What are resources? #Bell# Resources are things around us that we can use to create wealth. These are things we can use to earn a living. Examples of resources are; Soil, soil Water, water Wildlife, wildlife Land, land Minerals, minerals Forests, forests Can you identify any resources in your area? #Bell# Different Counties have different resources Which is the main resource in your county? Which is the main resource in your county? #Bell# Where do we get this resources? Where do we get this resources? #Bell# This resources are natural resources. Natural means God made. These are things that have not been made by man. Let us discuss some of these resources. WATER Where do you get water in your area? Where do you get water in your area? #Bell# Well done. I hope your answers include we get water from rivers, lakes and dams. We also collect water when it rains and store it in tanks for later use. Learner, which river is found in your county. Which river is found in your county? #Bell# Rivers and lakes provide us with water. People use water to: Drink Wash clothes and clean utensils and To take a bath, to take a bath Farmers use water to grow crops and give animals water to drink. In dry areas, we practice irrigation; this is using water to grow crops.

ANOTHER RESOURCE IS WILDLIFE. Wildlife refers to all the animals, birds and plants that are found in their natural environment. These natural environments include forest and water Which wild animals are found in your county? Which wild animals are found in your county? #Bell# Well done. I hope your answers include: 1. Lions. 2. Zebras. 3. Giraffes. 4. Rhinos. 5. Buffaloes. 6. Snakes. 7. Hyenas. 8. Elephants. 9. Wild beasts. 10. Hippos among many more. Learner, How does Wildlife help us to earn a living? How does Wildlife help us to earn a living? #Bell# Well done. Wild animals attract tourists. Tourists bring money to our country Who is a tourist? #Bell# A tourist is a person who travels from one place to another for pleasure. They visit places to; Interact with people to learn their culture. To watch birds and animals in their natural environment. They also visit places to see the beautiful sites and historic built environment. 3. FOREST ARE ANOTHER RESOURCE IN THE COUNTY Learner, what is a forest? #Bell# A forest is a large area covered by trees growing close together. Forests are mainly found in areas that receive a lot of rainfall. Some forests grow naturally while others are planted by people. The following are importance of forests. Forest provide home for wild animals Forest prevent soil erosion Trees in the forest provide us with wood used to make paper and furniture. Forest help us purify or clean up the air we breathe. Learner, How can we conserve the resources found in the county? How can we conserve the resources found in the county? #Bell# Resources can be conserved in the following ways. To conserve is to take good care of something while still using it. use water sparingly to avoid wastage. Use water sparingly to avoid wastage. Avoid cutting trees unnecessarily, when we cut a tree we should plant two for each cut tree. Conserve soil by planting trees to avoid soil erosion. Conserve soil by planting trees to avoid soil erosion To conserve wildlife stop poaching. To conserve wildlife stop poaching To conclude our lesson write a short report about the main resources in your county. And how you can conserve them. That marks the end of our lesson today. Until next time. Goodbye.

[ ] The radio presenter was teacher Esther Simaloi. Until next time. It is Goodbye. [ ]

SECTION 3: TRY THIS

1. Look again at the examples or pictures above.
2. Tell a parent or friend what Economic activities in the County means, using your own words.
3. Copy one example into your exercise book and change it to fit your school or home.
4. Underline three new words and find out what they mean.

SECTION 4: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Economic activities in the County.
2. Complete any “Work to do” items shown in the pupil book pages above.
3. Create three of your own practice questions on this topic.
4. Answer the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after finishing.

SECTION 5: REMEMBER
